messages:
Sam: Heads-up from today's micro-usability: in compact tables the kebab (⋯) feels tucked away when multi-select checkboxes are on. 3/5 testers missed it.
Priya: Which page? dashboard rules or incidents?
Sam: Rules table, compact density, narrow viewport. The three-dot visually aligns but the clickable rect is ~18px.
Jordan: Can we add an invisible hitpad instead of increasing visual chrome? Suggest token `--compact-action-hitpad: 6px` and use padding so icon stays 20px but target becomes ~32px.
Aisha: Accessibility: desktop 32px ok, mobile keep 44px. Ensure the kebab is a real `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and SR label e.g. "Actions for <rule name>". Menu items should be sentence case and verb-first.
Priya: Also toast placement is weird: they appear under the sticky filter and overlap controls. Copy is terse like "Deleted". Propose pattern: `"<Action> <object> — Undo"` (e.g., "Deleted 1 rule — Undo") and anchor toasts to page bottom-right on dense list pages.
Jordan: Implementation idea: add `.page-frame { position: relative; } .page-toasts { position: absolute; right: 24px; bottom: var(--toast-anchor-bottom, 24px); }` so pages opt in. Use `role="status" aria-live="polite"` for SR announcements.
Sam: CSS sketch for hitpad: `.action-btn { width:20px; height:20px; padding:var(--compact-action-hitpad); box-sizing: content-box; }` keeps visual size. For hover show subtle ghost bg and clear focus ring.
Aisha: Keyboard flow: Tab to row -> Tab to actions -> Enter to open -> Arrow to navigate -> Enter to select -> focus returns to opener. If we portal menu, return focus explicitly. Use `role="menu"` and `role="menuitem"`.
Priya: I like opt-in token and page-level toast container so other pages unaffected. I'll update copy guide with examples and SR phrasing.
Jordan: I'll open a tiny tokens PR: `tokens/interaction: add compact-action-hitpad=6px` and a small spacing token for toast offset.
deploy-bot: Preview build ready: https://preview.redwood/ui/compact-hitpad (branch: feat/compact-action-hitpad).
Sam: Can we run 6 short hallway sessions to validate discoverability, toast overlap, and keyboard flow?
Aisha: I'll run the sessions and document failures in the Figma accessibility notes.
Priya: If tests look good we ship token + toast container this sprint. Keep changes minimal and reversible. :thumbsup:
